steps.text: Sit or stand in a way that feels okay. Your eyes can stay open.
We'll breathe in for 4 and out for 6, a little longer on the way out.
Notice how you feel now. Any change is fine, and so is none.
If you feel dizzy, breathe normally.
If it feels okay, rest a hand on your chest or your arm.
Say to yourself: this hurts right now. Feeling hurt is part of being human.
Ask yourself: is there another way to read what happened? People are often busy, tired or caught up in their own day.
What would you say to a good friend who felt this way? Say it to yourself, in the same warm voice.
Try these words: I'm allowed to feel this. I still matter.
Look around. Name 5 things you can see.
Notice 4 things you can feel, like your feet on the floor or the fabric of your clothes.
Listen. Name 3 things you can hear.
Find 2 things you can smell, or think of 2 smells you like.
Name 1 thing you can taste, or take a sip of water.
Notice where you are sitting or standing. You're here, right now.
Skip this one if cold feels uncomfortable for you.
If you can, run cool water over your hands, or hold something cool for a moment.
Notice the coolness on your skin. Stay with it for a little while.
Say where you are, out loud or in your head.
Say what day it is today.
Name three things you can see right now.
You're here, in this place, on this day.
Strong feelings and urges rise like a wave, peak, and fall again. You don't have to act on this one.
Notice where you feel it in your body. Just notice it. There's nothing to change.
Stay with the wave for 90 seconds. Notice it rise and shift.
Notice how the wave is now. Whatever it's doing is okay.
Give the thought a short name, like "the argument" or "that message".
Pick a time later today or tomorrow to think about it. Picture setting it on a shelf until then.
Take one slow breath in, and let a long breath out.
It will keep until then. You can pick it up again at the time you chose.
